en.title: Calculate Mean and Mode
en.description:
Given an integer array, output two integers: the arithmetic mean rounded down, and the mode, the value that occurs most frequently. If there are several modes, return the smallest of them.

Original constraints: 1≤N≤100000, -10^9≤inputNums[i]≤10^9.

Original source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/cisco#9-calculate-mean-and-mode (fixed snapshot content fingerprint 82178bbe8b797598a998eeaf22296a73359f80847741be7e46723ab73ba1cc63). Another Fastprep record of the same problem does not state a tie rule for modes; this problem follows the smallest-value rule explicitly given on the original OAMaster problem page.
en.input: The first line contains N; the second line contains N integers inputNums[i].
en.output: Output `mean mode` in that order, as two integers separated by a space.
en.explanation: The mean is floor(sum(inputNums)/N); note that when a negative sum does not divide evenly, it rounds toward negative infinity. Use a frequency table to count the occurrences of each value, and take the smallest among the most frequent values.
hints: Integer division in Java/C++ truncates toward zero for negative numbers, so it cannot directly replace the mathematical floor.
For tied modes, return the smallest value as stated in the problem.
